standard.title: Community diversity and inclusion
standard.description: investigate strategies that influence how communities value diversity and propose actions they can take to promote inclusion in their communities
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have described and implemented strategies to value diversity in their communities (Y5-6). They can describe and implement strategies but have not yet been asked to investigate the broader mechanisms by which communities come to value diversity, or to propose community-level actions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate strategies that influence how communities value diversity and propose actions to promote inclusion in their communities.

nodes.label: Understanding diversity and its value
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what diversity means in community contexts, identify key dimensions of diversity relevant to their own community, and describe why valuing diversity matters for health and wellbeing.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what diversity means and describe at least one dimension of diversity in their community, giving one reason why valuing it matters for health and wellbeing.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe diversity across multiple dimensions (gender, race, sexuality, ability, cultural background); explain how valuing diversity contributes to individual and community health and wellbeing; examine how stereotypes, prejudice and discrimination undermine community health.
wider: Investigate how beliefs and cultural practices within, between and across cultural groups — including groups from the Asian region — have changed over time, and what has driven those changes
Examine how the concept of intersectionality (overlapping dimensions of diversity) affects how different individuals experience inclusion and exclusion

response_modes.reason: Diversity concepts become meaningful when grounded in multiple dimensions — students who only examine one type of diversity have a narrow basis for investigating community strategies.

success_criteria: Explains what diversity means in a community context
Identifies at least one dimension of diversity and explains why valuing it matters for health and wellbeing

nodes.label: Investigating strategies that promote community valuing of diversity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate specific strategies or initiatives that have influenced how communities value diversity, explaining the mechanisms by which they create change.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one strategy or initiative that influences how a community values diversity and explain how it works.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate strategies at multiple levels (school, local, national, global) that challenge stereotypes and promote inclusion; examine how norms and prejudice can be shifted; investigate events that value First Nations Australian contributions and strengthen relationships.
wider: Investigate events and strategies that value First Nations Australian contributions and strengthen relationships — such as Indigenous rounds in sporting codes and NAIDOC Week — evaluating the evidence for their effectiveness in shifting community attitudes
Research how anti-discrimination initiatives in different global contexts have addressed specific forms of prejudice, examining what made some more effective than others
nodes.hinge_reason: Proposing actions requires understanding how change happens — students who cannot explain the mechanisms by which strategies create shifts in community attitudes will propose actions without understanding why they would work.

response_modes.reason: When investigating strategies, explicitly ask students to identify the mechanism of change: who is the target of the strategy, what attitude or behaviour is being shifted, and how does the strategy produce that shift? This builds the causal reasoning needed for proposal.

Investigating strategies across diverse community contexts — including First Nations, Asian Australian, and other cultural community examples — builds a rich repertoire of approaches that informs more substantive proposal.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian community strategies and global comparison contexts provide genuine breadth that extends students' understanding well beyond their immediate social context — a meaningful development of social and civic literacy.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one strategy or initiative that influences community valuing of diversity
Explains the mechanism by which the strategy produces change

nodes.label: Proposing actions to promote inclusion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can propose specific, realistic actions to promote inclusion in their own communities, with reasoning that connects the proposed action to its intended effect.
nodes.minimum_width: Propose one action to promote inclusion in their community and explain why it would be effective.
nodes.typical_width: Propose a range of actions targeting different forms of discrimination or exclusion; connect proposals to the strategies investigated; explain how each proposed action would affect community inclusion; evaluate what is realistically achievable at student or school level.
wider: Develop strategies that directly challenge narrow views of gender, race, sexuality, gender diversity or ability in a school or community context, drawing on the investigation findings
Design and evaluate an inclusion initiative targeting a specific form of discrimination, using evidence from comparable campaigns to justify the design

response_modes.reason: Proposals integrate diversity concept understanding, strategy investigation and community analysis — instruction should position proposals as the culmination of investigation rather than a separate creative task.

success_criteria: Proposes at least one specific action to promote inclusion in their community
Explains why the action would be effective, connecting it to an identified mechanism of change
